chunks: that a number of people had their hands cut off in the way of Allah, and that everyone is distinguished (on that account),
but when the same thing occurred to one of us he was given the name “the flier in Paradise”; and “the two winged”!

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: In the way of Allah (for the sake of God)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the titles 'the flier' and 'the two-winged' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the selective honor bestowed upon the general companions for physical sacrifices, such as losing a hand in battle, while contrasting it with the diminished recognition accorded to the Ahl al-Bayt for their unique spiritual and physical trials. He specifically mocks the title 'al-Tayyar' (the flier) or 'Dhu al-Janahayn' (the two-winged) applied to Muawiya, highlighting the irony that a leader who caused the loss of a hand for the faith is celebrated with a somewhat trivial or ironic epithet, whereas the Imams' profound sacrifices are often overlooked or undervalued by the prevailing political narrative.
